instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell overhead with a close overhand grip and arms fully extended.
2. Keep your upper arms close to your head and stationary.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the barbell behind your head until your forearms are about parallel to the floor.
4. Press the barbell back up by extending your arms fully.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed and close to your head to isolate the triceps.
2. Move slowly and under control, especially while lowering.
3. Keep your core braced and avoid arching your lower back.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell at chest height with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders.
2. Brace your core and keep a neutral spine.
3. Press the barbell straight overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the barbell under control back to chest height.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to avoid arching your lower back.
2. Drive the bar in a straight line close to your face.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep wrists stacked over your forearms.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back with an overhand grip.
2. Brace your core and keep your hips facing forward.
3. Rotate your torso to the right under control.
4. Return to center, then rotate your torso to the left.
5. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Rotate from your torso, not just your arms.
2. Keep your hips and knees facing forward to isolate the obliques.
3. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
4. Exhale as you twist, inhale as you return to center.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip wider than shoulder-width.
2. Let your arms hang fully extended with the bar against your thighs.
3. Curl the barbell up by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the barbell under control to full extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows fixed at your sides to isolate the biceps.
2. Avoid swinging your body or using momentum.
3. Lower the bar slowly to keep tension on the muscle.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell at chest height with an overhand grip set just wider than shoulders.
2. Brace your core and keep a neutral spine.
3. Press the barbell straight overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the barbell under control back to chest height.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to protect your lower back.
2. Keep the bar path straight and close to your face.
3. Do not flare your elbows too far out at the bottom.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
